Sedgwick County at a glance

Wichita is the seat of Sedgwick County, which ranks second in Kansas by population. Residents numbered 523,824 in 2020 and an estimated 538,433 in 2025. Organized in 1867, the county measures 1,009 square miles, about 12 of them water.

It has twenty cities, from Wichita down to Viola, including Derby, Haysville, Goddard, Maize, Mulvane and Bel Aire. School districts only loosely follow city limits, and even neighbors on one street may end up in different districts. Look at your tax statement to see yours, because the school levy makes up a big share of the bill.

How the Appraiser notifies owners and takes appeals

Real property valuation notices go out from the County Appraiser on March 1. Without one in your mailbox, you can view and print it online, and the printout carries the appeal instructions.

Each tax year allows one appeal of your value. Return the informal appeal form printed on the back of the notice within 30 days, which usually means March 31. The office books a phone or in-person appointment and mails you the date about ten days ahead. Informal appeals are also heard in May and December.

When the informal meeting leaves the matter open, the Board of Tax Appeals Small Claims Division is the next stop. Single-family residences qualify, and so does non-agricultural property valued below $3 million, and fees may apply. Anyone representing you who is not an owner, immediate relative or attorney needs a declaration of representative form.

  • General appeal documents go to ApprHear@sedgwick.gov.
  • Commercial appeals go to ApprCom@sedgwick.gov.
  • Send evidence with it: comparable sales, photos and repair estimates.

Tax and appeal dates

The county works from a statutory calendar, and any deadline that falls on a weekend or holiday slides to the next business day.

EventDate
Valuation notices mailedMarch 1
Equalization appeal30 days from mailing
Informal meeting with appraiserMay 15
Appraiser final determinationMay 20
Appraiser certifies values to ClerkJune 1
Hearing officer or panel hearingsJuly 1
County Clerk certifies tax roll to TreasurerNovember 1
Tax statements mailedDecember 15
Full payment or first half dueDecember 20
Second half dueMay 10

Budgets from local governments reach the County Clerk by August 25, so final levies are set late in the year. Instead of an informal appeal, you may file a payment under protest form with the treasurer when you pay.

What happens when tax goes unpaid?

Real estate tax left unpaid can lead to a foreclosure auction. Under K.S.A. 79-2801, a county must foreclose on real estate with delinquent tax liens and sell it at public auction.

Parcels whose taxes have run two and a half or three and a half years behind are chosen by the Treasurer's office. Each chosen parcel picks up a $400 first foreclosure fee, which landed on October 1 in 2026.

  • After a District Court case begins, redeeming means paying every delinquent year, plus interest and fees, in cash or certified funds.
  • Owners, heirs and lienholders of record may redeem until the close of business on the day before the sale.
  • You can sell privately before the auction, but that is a matter between you and your buyer. A newly recorded deed does not halt the case. Paying in full does.
  • After a sale, owners or lienholders can challenge it in District Court.
  • Auction buyers owe the full tax for the year of sale and any special assessments, but not the delinquent taxes, and a $21 deed filing fee is due at checkout.
  • Deeds usually arrive about 120 days after the sale, and the county is not responsible for evicting occupants.

Each month's delinquent amount holds if paid by 5 p.m. on the 20th, and interest accrues afterward. Unrelated to land, unpaid personal property tax blocks vehicle tag renewal, and a court warrant can follow if it remains unpaid by October 20.

Recording a sale

A deed goes to the Register of Deeds together with a Kansas Real Estate Sales Validation Questionnaire. The County Clerk then logs the transfer for tax purposes and keeps the owner's mailing address on the tax system.

Which deed form fits your sale is a question for a real estate attorney or title company. Phone numbers: Register of Deeds 316-660-9400, County Clerk 316-660-9200, Treasurer 316-660-9000.

Ask the County Clerk or your city clerk about special assessments before closing. Those are tracked apart from the general levy.

After you move, remember that the tax system holds an owner's mailing address. If you keep the house until it sells, make sure the County Clerk has an address where you actually receive mail, so a December statement or a delinquency notice does not go to an empty house. For an inherited property, the heirs should update that address as soon as they take charge, because the redemption rules count heirs among those who can act.

Which Sedgwick County sellers run into trouble?

The most urgent cases are houses with several years of unpaid tax, because the foreclosure clock runs on the two and a half and three and a half year marks. Inherited houses come next, since heirs are among those who may redeem. And owners who miss the 30-day informal appeal window have less room that year, because a value can be appealed only once.

  • Get the delinquent balance from the Treasurer before you set a price.
  • Find out whether special assessments are attached to the parcel.
  • Decide early whether to appeal the notice, because the appeal is limited to one per tax year.

To talk through a sale, send the address of your Sedgwick County house and we will describe what a cash offer could involve.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Sedgwick County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Steps for selling with a tax problem

  1. Phone the Treasurer, 316-660-9000, for the delinquent balance with interest and fees.
  2. Ask if a foreclosure case is on file in District Court, since that changes the redemption terms.
  3. Ask about special assessments at the County Clerk, 316-660-9200, or at your city clerk.
  4. Pick a buyer and a title company. At closing the title company pays the tax balance from the proceeds, and that payment in full is what ends the matter.
  5. Record the deed and the Sales Validation Questionnaire with the Register of Deeds, 316-660-9400.

A large balance makes timing critical. Payment in full halts foreclosure and a new deed alone does not, so schedule the closing to pay what is owed ahead of the day before the auction. Keep copies of the payoff letter and the closing statement. If a buyer asks later about the lien or the case, those papers answer it. A seller who has them can also show clearly that the county's claim was paid in full on a specific date.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I appeal a Sedgwick County property valuation?

Begin at the Sedgwick County Appraiser's Office. The form on the back of your March 1 notice is due within 30 days, usually March 31.

When is Sedgwick County property tax due?

Statements arrive by December 15. Pay everything or the first half by December 20, then the second half by May 10.

How long can taxes go unpaid before foreclosure in Sedgwick County?

Parcels two and a half or three and a half years behind are selected. If nobody redeems, a District Court case leads to auction.

Can I sell my Sedgwick County house if taxes are delinquent?

Yes. A closing that pays the balance in full halts foreclosure. A recorded deed by itself does not.

What forms are filed when a Sedgwick County house sells?

The deed and a Kansas Real Estate Sales Validation Questionnaire go to the Register of Deeds, and then the County Clerk updates the tax record.

Selling in Johnson County? Get a Cash Offer

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Johnson County?
We buy Johnson County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Johnson County at a glance

Johnson County, Kansas, is run from Olathe. Its 476 square miles were part of the Shawnee Indian Reservation until it opened to settlement in 1854, and territorial lawmakers formed the county on August 25, 1855. About 636,906 people lived here in mid-2025, and the median household income is $109,208.

The larger cities are Overland Park, Olathe, Shawnee, Lenexa, Leawood, Prairie Village, Gardner, Merriam and Mission. They share one appraiser and one treasurer, yet each lies in different school and special taxing districts. Similar houses a few miles apart can therefore get quite different bills, which is why your own statement is the thing to read.

How the tax bill is calculated

The formula starts with assessed value times the combined mill levy. Special assessments are added, and the school general credit is subtracted.

Assessed value is only a share of appraised value: 11.5% for residential property and 25% for commercial. A mill is $1 of tax for each $1,000 of assessed value.

  • County taxing district: 17.276 mills in 2025 and 17.263 in the 2026 budget.
  • Library district: 3.812 mills in both years.
  • Park and recreation district: 3.018 mills in 2025 and 3.020 in 2026.
  • Everything else: a city, a school district and any special districts each add a levy on top of the county's 24.110 mills for 2025.

For tax years 2024 and 2025 the school general credit was $172.50, reflecting $8,625 of residential assessed value that escapes the 20 mill school general levy. Property that is not residential gets no credit.

Tax dates

Three dates anchor the year: January 1, December 20 and May 10. Values are set as of January 1, notices follow by March 1, and payment comes in two halves.

DateWhat happens
January 1Appraisal year valuation date
On or before March 1Notices of Appraised Value go out
30 days after mailingInformal appeal deadline; the county lists on or before March 31
Mid-NovemberFirst-half notices go out
December 20Full payment or first half is due
Beginning of AprilSecond-half notices go out
May 10Second half is due
May 15 and May 20Informal real property appeals wrap up, and decisions go out by May 20

One property tax division acts as County Clerk and Treasurer. Email taxinfo@jocogov.org, call 913-715-2600, or stop by 111 S. Cherry St., Suite 1200, Olathe, on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Johnson County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to appeal your appraisal

You get a single protest for each tax year. Pick either an informal appeal in the spring or a payment under protest at billing time. Filing both for one year is not allowed.

  • Informal appeal: return the form printed on the back of your Notice of Appraised Value, or use the online portal, within 30 days of mailing.
  • Payment under protest: give the treasurer the protest form by December 20 when you pay yourself, by January 31 when a mortgage company pays, or by May 10 for second-half or late full payments.
  • Hearing: choose a short phone call, a short meeting in person, or a paper review of your written evidence. Each phone or in-person slot lasts 20 minutes.
  • Next level: a further appeal goes to the State Board of Tax Appeals, in its Small Claims Division or Regular Division, within 30 days of the mailing date.

State rules have the appraiser view every property at least once in six years, combining an interview, an exterior inspection and computer-generated data. A cracked foundation can lower a value and a finished basement can raise it, so photograph both before a sale. The Appraiser's Office posts the forms on its property value appeals page.

What happens when Johnson County tax goes unpaid?

Missed real estate tax first earns interest, then publication, then a lien, and finally a tax foreclosure auction. Parcels still unpaid on July 31 appear in the newspaper, with a $15 publication fee. A lien goes on the first Tuesday in September, which starts the redemption period.

When redemption ends with taxes still owing, the county sues to foreclose and sells the property at auction. Owners can still redeem by paying every tax and cost before 5:00 p.m. on the day before the sale. Winning bidders pay everything that day in cash or certified funds, and a bidder with delinquent Johnson County tax is barred.

Four to six weeks after the auction the court holds a confirmation hearing, and the Sheriff issues a deed roughly 30 days later. Money left over after taxes and costs goes to the court. Owners who are behind and cannot list in time sometimes turn to a direct buyer.

Recording a deed

Recording starts at $21 for the first page of a deed or mortgage, plus $17 for every added page, under K.S.A. 28-115. The Register of Deeds accepts cash, check, money order, cashier's check or card, with a 2.25% card processing add-on.

  • Mortgage release: $16 a page, plus $4 for book and page.
  • Non-federal lis pendens: $8. Releasing a lis pendens is free.
  • Abstract of judgment: $17.
  • Mechanic's lien: $17.
  • Sales validation questionnaire: free.

Page one needs a 3 inch top margin, other margins are 1 inch, and type cannot be smaller than 8 point. Call 913-715-0775 or visit 111 S. Cherry St., Suite 1200, Olathe. Any lien or judgment recorded against the house turns up in the title search, so plan to pay it off at closing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Johnson County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Tax relief and refunds

Kansas offers three state refund programs, Homestead, SAFESR and SVR. File each claim with the state between January 1 and April 15 every year. Because the state pays the refund, the bill Johnson County mails in November stays the same.

Paid the wrong parcel, or paid twice? Only the person who paid may ask for a refund or transfer. Current-year requests are due March 15 for a first-half payment and June 25 for a second-half payment, and a delinquent-year request must arrive within 45 days of payment.

Selling a Johnson County house with taxes owed

Back taxes do not rule out a sale. They come out of your proceeds at closing together with interest. Work through it in this order.

  1. Ask the property tax division at 913-715-2600 for the exact amount owed, including interest.
  2. Find out whether the parcel has been published or has a lien, because that sets your timetable.
  3. If a foreclosure case is open, redemption has to happen before 5:00 p.m. on the day before the auction.
  4. Have the title company confirm that special assessments and recorded liens will be paid at the table.

A cash buyer can close quickly and accept the house in its current state, which helps if a published list or a hearing date is looming. Whether the offer works is your decision, and a sale that pays all that is owed ends the tax problem.

Frequently asked questions

When is Johnson County property tax due?

Either pay everything by December 20 or split it, with half on December 20 and half on May 10 of the following year. Notices for the first half arrive in mid-November and for the second at the start of April.

How long do I have to appeal my Johnson County valuation?

Thirty days from the mailing date of the Notice of Appraised Value, which the county lists as on or before March 31. A payment under protest follows separate dates: December 20, January 31 or May 10.

Can I sell a Johnson County house with delinquent tax?

Yes, as long as tax and interest are cleared by closing. For a parcel already in foreclosure, redemption has to come before 5:00 p.m. the day before the auction.

Where do I record a deed in Johnson County?

Take it to the Register of Deeds, 111 S. Cherry St., Suite 1200, Olathe. Page one costs $21 and each added page $17.

Do tax relief programs lower my Johnson County bill?

No. Homestead, SAFESR and SVR are refunds the state pays after you file between January 1 and April 15, and the county's bill is unchanged.

Wyandotte County basics

Wyandotte County is the smallest county in Kansas, at 156 square miles, and it shares one unified government with its county seat, Kansas City, Kansas. The 2020 population was 169,245. Four cities sit inside the county line: Kansas City, Bonner Springs, Edwardsville and Lake Quivira, which also reaches into Johnson County.

Four school districts cover the county: Turner USD 202, Piper USD 203, Bonner Springs-Edwardsville USD 204 and Kansas City USD 500. Each carries its own value and levy, so the district on your parcel changes the bill.

Because the county is small, one appraiser and one treasurer cover every address, from the river neighborhoods to the interstate retail area.

Who does what: the county offices

The Appraiser values property and the Treasury bills and collects. The Appraiser's page says the office does not set or collect taxes. Taxing districts do that through their budgets, which become the levy.

OfficeAddressPhone
Appraiser's Office (County Annex)8200 State Ave, Kansas City, KS 66112(913) 573-8400
Treasury, downtown710 N 7th St, Kansas City, KS 66101(913) 573-2823
Treasury, annex (drop box)8200 State AveSame as downtown
Delinquent Real EstateCourthouse, 710 N 7th St, Suite 200(913) 573-2817

The Appraiser's Office is open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Pay online through the myWyco site or app, in person (cash, check, money order, or Visa, MasterCard and Discover), by mail with a check or money order, or in the drop box. Payments by phone are not accepted.

Due dates and penalties

The first half is due December 20 and the second half is due May 10. Taxes become a lien on the real estate on November 1. About then each parcel is mailed a tax bill and an information sheet comparing this year's values, rates and taxes with the year before. Parcels with a mortgage escrow get only the information sheet. Not getting a bill does not excuse late payment.

  • If the total tax is at least $10, you can pay in halves without interest.
  • A second-half bill goes out around April 1 to people who paid the first half.
  • Partial payments are accepted, but the unpaid part of the first half keeps accruing interest.
  • Parcels still unpaid on July 25 get a $16 advertising fee and are advertised in August.
  • On the first Tuesday in September, unpaid properties are "sold" to the county, which turns the taxes from current to delinquent.

Call the Treasury for the current interest rate before you compute a payoff.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Wyandotte County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How a Wyandotte County tax bill is calculated

The appraiser sets value, then each taxing government sets a budget and a mill rate. Residential property is assessed at 11.5% of appraised value, and one mill is $1 of tax per $1,000 of assessed value.

Houses get a break on the school levy. The first $20,000 of a home's appraised value is not subject to the school general levy, so a $100,000 home has two assessed values: $11,500 for most levies and $9,200 for the school general levy. The state sets three levies on its own: 1 mill for educational buildings, one-half mill for correctional buildings, and 40 mills for schools.

Property inside USD 500 also supports the Kansas City, Kansas Public Library, while the rest of the county outside USD 500 and Bonner Springs pays a separate library levy. For current rates, read your own statement or ask the Treasury.

How to appeal your Wyandotte County valuation

File an informal appeal by the date printed on your valuation notice. Notices are mailed in late February with a deadline about a month later. The Appraiser notes that most owners should expect an increase because of limited housing supply, stronger demand and revitalization in parts of the county.

The office lists two reasons for an appeal: the appraised value is higher than the property could reasonably sell for, or the property classification is wrong.

Appeals can go in online, by hand or by mail to the Annex. Meetings can be by phone, on submitted evidence only, virtual or in person. Useful evidence includes a recent fee appraisal, photos of interior or structural problems, and recent sales of comparable properties.

One warning matters a lot: if you start an informal appeal and then abandon it, you cannot pay under protest or appeal again for the same property and tax year. If you miss the deadline, the second chance is a Payment Under Protest, filed in writing with the Treasurer by December 20, or by January 31 if an escrow agent pays at least half. It cannot be used if you already appealed that year, and a first-half protest rules out a second protest for the second half.

Kansas also gives a route to the Board of Tax Appeals within 30 days of the informal decision. The state calendar puts the informal meeting window at May 13 and the final determination at May 20.

When Wyandotte County sells houses for unpaid tax

The Unified Government holds two public auctions a year for tax-sale eligible property. Eligibility depends on the type of property:

  • Homestead properties: delinquent taxes for at least three years
  • Commercial properties: at least two years
  • Vacant and abandoned properties: at least one year

The delinquency count starts on the first Tuesday in September of the year after the levy year. Being eligible does not mean a parcel will be included, since only a limited number go into each sale. Delinquent payments are applied to the most recent delinquent year first, under Charter Resolution CR-01-12.

If you own a vacant or abandoned lot or house, that one-year clock is much shorter than the homestead clock, so check the list sooner rather than later.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Wyandotte County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling a Wyandotte County house with taxes due

Back taxes are a lien, and a title company can pay them from the sale proceeds at closing. Before you list or accept an offer, collect these items:

  1. The parcel number and a current balance from the myWyco site or the Treasury.
  2. Whether the parcel is on the tax sale list, and the date of the next auction.
  3. Any pending appeal, since abandoning one closes off a later protest.
  4. A payoff figure that runs to the closing date, because interest and the August advertising fee change the total.

Cash Home Buyers reviews Wyandotte County houses as they stand, including those with unpaid tax. You decide whether the written offer works against your payoff.

What happens at closing

The title company checks the record for liens and unpaid taxes, prepares the deed and totals what comes out of your proceeds. You sign the deed at closing, and the current year's tax is divided between you and the buyer. Bring photo ID and every key, and if a mortgage is open, ask the lender for a payoff figure ahead of time.

Frequently asked questions

Who sends the property tax bill in Wyandotte County?

The Unified Government Treasury sends it. The county Appraiser's Office values the property but does not set or collect the tax.

When is the first half of Wyandotte County property tax due?

December 20. The second half is due May 10, and halves are allowed without interest when the total tax is at least $10.

What is the Wyandotte County appeal deadline?

It is the date printed on your valuation notice. Notices are mailed in late February, and the deadline falls about a month later.

How long before Wyandotte County can sell a house at a tax sale?

For homestead property, delinquent taxes must be at least three years old. Commercial property needs two years and vacant or abandoned property needs one.

Do Wyandotte County homeowners get a school tax break?

Yes. The first $20,000 of a residence's appraised value is not subject to the school general levy, so a house carries two assessed values.

Pottawatomie County at a glance

Pottawatomie County lies in northeastern Kansas between Manhattan and Topeka. It covers 862 square miles, of which 841 are land. Westmoreland is the county seat and Wamego is the largest city. Territorial lawmakers created the county in 1857 out of land that had belonged to Riley County.

The 2020 census counted 25,348 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 27,186. The county has kept adding people while many rural Kansas counties shrink, and local planners project a population above 36,000 by 2044. Much of the land is farmland dotted with small towns, with manufacturing, trade, transport, health care and private education among the leading industries.

Your tax bill depends on the city and school district your parcel falls into, so start there.

Cities and school districts

The county's cities are Belvue, Emmett, Havensville, Louisville, Manhattan, Olsburg, Onaga, St. George, St. Marys, Wamego, Westmoreland and Wheaton. Manhattan and St. Marys also extend into adjacent counties. Wamego had 4,841 residents in 2020 and sits where U.S. 24 meets K-99, roughly 14 miles east of Manhattan.

Four unified districts are based in the county: Wamego USD 320, Kaw Valley USD 321, Onaga USD 322 and Rock Creek USD 323. Other districts, including Manhattan-Ogden USD 383, have offices in neighboring counties, so confirm the district for your parcel on your tax statement.

One local quirk catches sellers off guard. Green Valley, near Manhattan, carries a Manhattan mailing address although it is outside the city limits. A house there is taxed, permitted and inspected under county rules, not by the City of Manhattan.

How valuations and notices work

The County Appraiser lists and values every parcel, and notices of value for real property go out by March 1. State law requires the appraiser to view and inspect all property once every six years, though inspections can happen more often.

The appraiser does not simply use what you paid. One sale carries weight, but the appraiser has to decide whether it was an arm's length deal and then compare similar sales. Values are set as of January 1 each year, so a house you bought in the summer is still valued against that earlier date.

A higher value does not automatically raise your bill. What you owe depends on the budgets of the local governments that tax your parcel, special assessments and the state school levy. The County Clerk divides each unit's budget need by the assessed value in its area to arrive at the mill levy, then certifies the tax roll to the Treasurer.

How to appeal a valuation

Contact the County Appraiser's Office within 30 days of the date the notice was mailed. The informal meeting deadline is May 15, and Hearing Officer or Panel hearings finish by July 1.

A second route is a payment under protest. File the form with the County Treasurer when you pay, no later than December 20. If an escrow or tax service agent pays for you by that date, the deadline moves to January 31. Once you appeal the notice of value, you cannot pay under protest for the same parcel and year, so pick one path.

  • Ask the appraiser for the Property Record Card and check bedrooms, baths and square footage.
  • Request the comparable sales sheet, which lists up to five similar homes.
  • Bring photos, repair estimates for structural damage, a recent fee appraisal or a sales contract from the last two to three years.
  • If a non-attorney will speak for you, complete the Declaration of Representation form.

At a small claims hearing run by the State Board of Tax Appeals, the county has to prove its value is right.

Tax calendar

The first half, or the full amount, is due on or before December 20, and the second half is due by May 10 of the following year.

StepDate
Valuation notices mailedBy March 1
Informal meeting with County AppraiserMay 15
Hearing Officer or Panel hearings finishedJuly 1
First half or full payment dueDecember 20
Second half dueMay 10 of the next year

Who pays the tax when a house sells mid-year?

Unless the contract says otherwise, the buyer owes the tax on real property sold on or after January 1 and before November 1. The seller owes it if the sale closes on or after November 1 and before January 1. The rule comes from K.S.A. 79-1805.

Property is not prorated on the tax roll when it changes hands (K.S.A. 79-309). Many purchase contracts prorate anyway, which is why a settlement statement often shows a credit or a charge for taxes. A cash buyer and a seller can agree on this in writing, and the county treats the private contract as controlling.

If you sell around November or December, look at the timing closely. Under the default rule a seller who closes in late November owes that year's bill, and the December 20 deadline is only weeks away.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Pottawatomie County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Building and land rules

County building codes apply only inside the Blue Township Sewer District, which includes Green Valley, and have applied there since January 1, 2020. Outside that district, it is the buyer's job to check the quality of construction.

Zoning is also unusual. When countywide zoning started in 1972, nearly all of the county was zoned A1, agriculture, so even a single-family home can require a rezoning. For rural lots, the rule of thumb is a minimum of 3 acres with a rural or city water district and a private septic system, or 5 acres with a private well and septic.

  • A permit is needed for houses, additions, moved-in homes and manufactured homes. Sheds of 120 square feet or less and fences do not need one.
  • Any type of manufactured home may go on an operating farm of 40 acres or more for the owner, a blood relative or an employee.
  • Rural burn permits apply only in unincorporated areas. Cities such as Wamego and Westmoreland follow their own rules.
  • Green Valley has no adopted nuisance code, so overgrown grass or noise are not covered by county resolutions.

Deeds and liens at the Register of Deeds

Documents are recorded the same day the Register of Deeds receives them, once the office has checked them for completeness, assessed the fee and scanned them. No document is filed until the fee is paid.

The office holds many liens, including UCC filings and federal and state tax liens, but not all of them. Check with the Clerk of the District Court and the Kansas Department of Revenue for others. The Register of Deeds is also the office to call about restrictive covenants in a subdivision.

Before closing, pull the title history, confirm special assessments with the county Administration Office and settle any lien you find.

What sellers usually face

Plan for private wells and septic systems, agricultural zoning, a school district that may differ from the mailing address, and closing dates that fall near the December 20 and May 10 payment dates.

  • Inherited farmhouses where the title is not yet clear.
  • Manufactured homes placed under older county rules.
  • Green Valley houses that carry a Manhattan address but follow county rules.
  • Owners who missed the 30-day appeal window and want to know what comes next.

If one of these fits your house, send us the address and we will explain how a cash sale would work. A cash buyer can take a rural house as it stands, including one with an older septic system or unclear zoning, and the title company settles any taxes or liens from the proceeds.

Frequently asked questions

Who do I call about a Pottawatomie County valuation?

Call the County Appraiser's Office within 30 days of the mailing date printed on your notice. The County Treasurer handles payment under protest and the bill itself.

Does Pottawatomie County prorate property tax at closing?

Not on the tax roll. Property is not prorated off or onto the roll, though private contracts commonly prorate. Check your sales contract to see who owes what.

What is the deadline to pay Pottawatomie County property tax?

The first half or the full amount is due December 20, and the second half is due May 10 of the following year.

Can I sell a house in Pottawatomie County with taxes still owed?

Yes. Unpaid taxes are a lien that is cleared at closing from the proceeds, so the buyer receives clean title. Confirm the balance with the Treasurer before you set a closing date.

Do county building codes apply to every Pottawatomie County house?

No. The county has adopted building codes only inside the Blue Township Sewer District. Elsewhere in the county, the buyer is responsible for checking construction quality.

Sumner County at a glance

Sumner County sits in south-central Kansas on the Oklahoma line, with Wellington as the county seat and largest city. It had 22,382 residents in 2020. The courthouse is at 501 N. Washington, Wellington, KS 67152, and the Register of Deeds can be reached at (620) 326-2041.

The incorporated cities are Argonia, Belle Plaine, Caldwell, Conway Springs, Geuda Springs, Hunnewell, Mayfield, Milan, Mulvane, Oxford, South Haven and Wellington. The county also has 30 townships, which matters because township and special-district levies change a rural bill.

A town house in Wellington or Mulvane often attracts commuters, while an acreage or farm house near Caldwell or Argonia draws a smaller, more specialized group of buyers.

School districts and your tax bill

Twelve unified school districts reach into the county, and the one that serves a parcel sets a large part of its bill. They are Mulvane USD 263, Clearwater USD 264, Kingman-Norwich USD 331, Wellington USD 353, Conway Springs USD 356, Belle Plaine USD 357, Oxford USD 358, Argonia USD 359, Caldwell USD 360, South Haven USD 509, Arkansas City USD 470 and Udall USD 463.

School levies in 2025 run from 43.329 mills for the Arkansas City district to 74.411 for Caldwell, with Wellington at 50.863. Two houses of similar value can carry noticeably different bills only because of where the district line runs.

Mill levies by city

Every parcel carries a combined county and state levy of 51.537 mills, made up of a 50.037 county levy and a 1.500 state levy. City, township, school and special-district levies are added on top. The totals below already include every layer for that location.

City2025 total levy (mills)
Wellington169.563
Mulvane172.621
Oxford163.538
South Haven169.839
Belle Plaine189.460
Caldwell245.767
Argonia162.099

Rural parcels have their own tax-unit codes. A parcel near Wellington Township in the Wellington school district carries 139.157 mills, while one in Morris Township in the Caldwell school district carries 245.821. Find the unit code on your tax statement and match it to the county's levy sheet page.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Sumner County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How the appraiser values a house

The county appraiser values every parcel as of January 1 at fair market value, using the cost approach and the sales approach for residential property. The income approach is not used for houses because there is not enough data to apply it efficiently.

Fair market value in Kansas means the amount a well-informed buyer is justified in paying and a well-informed seller is justified in accepting in an open and competitive market, without undue compulsion. A variance of 10% above or below market value is not treated as a violation under K.S.A. 79-1426.

Disasters follow a specific rule. If a house burns or is damaged by a tornado, wind, flood or vandalism, it is still valued as it stood on January 1 of the tax year, even if the damage happened on January 2, and the tax is not due until December 20. If you sell a storm-damaged house mid-year, expect the bill to reflect the earlier condition.

Appraisal dates and appeal steps

Real estate valuation notices go out March 1, real property appeals are due March 30, and informal conferences finish by May 15 with decisions mailed by May 20.

  • January 1: valuation date for real and personal property.
  • March 1: real estate valuation notices mailed.
  • March 30: deadline to file real property appeals.
  • May 15: informal valuation conferences completed, and personal property appeals due.
  • June 15: appraiser certifies the roll to the county clerk.
  • December 20: first-half payment under protest deadline.

You may appeal once a year, either after the notice or when you pay the tax. Appeal if you could not sell the house for the value shown. Bring photographs of damage, sales of similar properties and a list of questions. Sales information is open to the public from March 31 through May 15 for owners considering an appeal.

Recording deeds and estate papers

The Sumner County Register of Deeds, on the first floor of the courthouse in Wellington, records every real estate transaction in the county. The fee is $21.00 for the first page of a deed, mortgage, oil and gas lease, affidavit or death certificate and $17.00 for each additional page.

A mortgage release or assignment costs $20.00 for the first page that releases one book and page, plus $4.00 for each extra page. An extra $16.00 applies for each additional book and page released in the same document. When an estate sells a house, a death certificate or affidavit often goes into the record alongside the deed. For title insurance or an abstract update, the office refers you to local title companies.

Selling an inherited or rural property

Rural and small-town sellers deal with inherited houses, farm parcels with outbuildings and storm damage. A cash buyer can skip the appraisal and repair negotiation that tend to stall those sales.

  • Different levies: a rural tax unit can carry a much higher total than a Wellington address.
  • Estate records: collect the death certificate, any affidavits and the deed before you call anyone.
  • Storm damage: the appraiser values the property as of January 1, so keep photographs and repair estimates.
  • Payment timing: December 20 and May 10 are the two tax dates to plan a closing around.

Use the Sumner County offices and levy sheet for your own parcel.

What to expect between offer and closing

After you accept an offer, the title company checks the record for liens and unpaid taxes and prepares the deed. They add up what comes out of your proceeds, including any mortgage payoff and the current tax bill, which is divided between you and the buyer. At closing you sign the deed and it goes to the Register of Deeds for recording. Bring photo ID and every key, and for an estate bring proof of who may sign.

Taxes owed when the house sells

Tax on a house stays with the property until it is paid. If you sell before the December 20 or May 10 dates, the title company will ask for the current balance and settle it from your proceeds. Keep the latest statement, and the unit code printed on it, so the title company can confirm which levies apply to your parcel.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

When a cash sale fits

A cash buyer takes the house as it stands, which suits storm damage, outbuildings that need work or an estate that wants a quick close. If a house is in good shape and you have time, a listing may bring more offers. Contact us with the parcel address and we will compare both routes honestly.

Frequently asked questions

What is the county seat of Sumner County, Kansas?

Wellington, which is also the largest city. The courthouse is at 501 N. Washington in Wellington.

What is the Sumner County mill levy?

The 2025 county levy is 50.037 mills and the state levy is 1.500 mills, for 51.537 combined. City, school, township and special-district levies are added on top, so 2025 total rates by city range from 162.099 mills in Argonia to 245.767 in Caldwell.

When is the deadline to appeal a Sumner County valuation?

March 30 is the deadline to file real property appeals. Informal conferences are completed by May 15, and decisions are mailed by May 20.

How much does it cost to record a deed in Sumner County?

$21.00 for the first page and $17.00 for each additional page. The same fee applies to mortgages, affidavits and death certificates.

Is a damaged house valued lower in Sumner County?

Not for the current tax year. A property damaged by fire, tornado, wind, flood or vandalism is still valued as it stood on January 1, even if the damage happens the next day.
